subject: General Knowledge and Current Affairs
curriculum: NOT an official ZIMSEC/MoPSE subject - this is a supplementary content file for general knowledge quizzes, current affairs discussion, and trivia at primary-school level, requested separately from the official curriculum files.
confidence_flag: Current-affairs facts (office-holders, current records, etc.) are accurate as of this file's generation date and were verified via web search, but they WILL go stale over time - office-holders change, records get broken. chunks.content: As of this file's generation: the President of Zimbabwe is Emmerson Mnangagwa (in office since 24 November 2017, re-elected 2023). The First Vice-President is Constantino Chiwenga, and the Second Vice-President is Kembo Mohadi. Zimbabwe's ruling party is ZANU-PF. This information changes with elections and cabinet reshuffles and should be re-verified periodically rather than assumed to remain current indefinitely.

Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in Southern Africa, bordered by Zambia (north), Mozambique (east), South Africa (south), and Botswana (west/southwest). Its capital city is Harare. Its official languages include English, Shona, and Ndebele, among 16 officially recognised languages under the 2013 Constitution. Its national symbols include the National Flag, the Zimbabwe Bird, and the national flower, which is the Flame Lily. Its currency is the ZiG (Zimbabwe Gold), introduced in 2024. Victoria Falls, one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, sits on the Zambezi River on Zimbabwe's border with Zambia. Great Zimbabwe, the stone ruins of a medieval city, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the country's namesake ('Zimbabwe' derives from 'dzimba dzemabwe', Shona for 'houses of stone').

Zimbabwe's economy relies heavily on agriculture and mining. Its major mineral exports include gold, platinum, diamonds, and lithium. The main agricultural crops are tobacco, maize (the staple food), cotton, and sugar cane. The Kariba Dam on the Zambezi River is a major source of hydroelectric power for the country and is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world.

The seven continents are: Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Antarctica, and Australia/Oceania. Asia is the largest continent by both area and population. Africa is the second largest continent and the world's second most populous, and is the continent Zimbabwe is part of.

The five oceans, from largest to smallest, are: the Pacific Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, the Indian Ocean, the Southern (Antarctic) Ocean, and the Arctic Ocean. The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean in the world.

The longest river in the world is the Nile River (in Africa, flowing through countries including Egypt and Sudan), though some measurements place the Amazon River as longer depending on methodology. The tallest mountain above sea level is Mount Everest (in the Himalayas, on the border of Nepal and China/Tibet). The largest desert (hot desert) is the Sahara Desert in Africa; the largest desert overall (including cold deserts) is Antarctica. The largest country by area is Russia; the most populous country is India (which overtook China in population around 2023).

chunks.topic: Basic Facts About the Human Body and Animals
chunks.content: The human body has 206 bones in adulthood (infants are born with about 270-300 bones, many of which fuse together during growth). The heart is roughly the size of a closed fist and beats around 100,000 times per day. The largest organ in the human body is the skin. The cheetah is the fastest land animal, capable of speeds up to about 100-120 km/h in short bursts. The blue whale is the largest animal to have ever lived on Earth, larger than any known dinosaur.

There are eight planets in our solar system: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Jupiter is the largest planet; Mercury is the smallest and closest to the Sun. Earth is the only known planet with life. The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, and it takes about 27.3 days to orbit the Earth. A light-year is a unit of distance (not time) - the distance light travels in one year, roughly 9.46 trillion kilometres.

chunks.topic: Popular Sports in Zimbabwe and Major Sporting Events
chunks.content: Football (soccer) is the most widely played and watched sport in Zimbabwe, with the national team nicknamed 'The Warriors'. Cricket is also popular, with Zimbabwe holding Test cricket status and having competed in multiple Cricket World Cups. Rugby, netball, athletics and boxing are also significant sports in the country. The FIFA World Cup (football) is held every 4 years; the Summer and Winter Olympic Games are each held every 4 years (staggered two years apart). The Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) is the top international football competition for African national teams.

The United Nations (UN) was founded in 1945, after the Second World War, to promote international peace and cooperation; Zimbabwe is a UN member state. The African Union (AU), founded in 2002 (succeeding the earlier Organisation of African Unity, founded 1963), promotes unity and cooperation among African states; its headquarters are in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a regional body of Southern African countries, including Zimbabwe, promoting regional economic and political cooperation.

There are 7 days in a week, 12 months in a year, and (usually) 365 days in a year, with an extra day (366 days total, 29 February) in a leap year, which occurs every 4 years (with some exceptions for century years not divisible by 400). The primary colours (in traditional colour theory used in art) are red, blue and yellow, which can be mixed to create secondary colours (green, orange, purple). Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and freezes at 0 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure (sea level).
